title: Predictive Warm Pools + Policy Composer for Tenant Latency Budgets
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level PRD for implementing predictive warm pools (forecast-driven prewarm of reserved capacity) and a Policy Composer UI that lets operators bind latency budgets, cost ceilings, and isolation preferences to tenant groups. This feature aims to reduce cold-start latency and avoid emergency over-provisioning while giving tenants predictable latency under bursty traffic patterns.
background: Customers on Dedicated want low tail latency for production LLM traffic but also predictable monthly costs. Current approaches use static reserved pools or manual pre-warming which either wastes capacity or fails to meet tight latency SLOs during sudden surges. Prior PRDs cover reserve pools and burst handoffs; this initiative combines short-term forecasting with policy-based routing/fallbacks to reduce both cost and P99 latency regressions.
goals: Reduce cold-start/first-token P99 latency for bursty tenants by 30% vs today
Provide a composable Policy Composer in Console to declare tenant latency budgets, cost ceilings, and preferred fallback models
Automate warm pool sizing with short-horizon forecasts (0-60 minutes) and safe fallback actions
Ensure predictable billing signals: track warm-pool cost vs saved tail-latency incidents
non_goals: Replace long-term capacity forecasting used for reservations (monthly reserves)
Full cross-region active-active warm replication (out of scope for initial rollouts)
Deep model-quality re-ranking as part of fallback (we will use compatible model variants only)
requirements: Runtime: expose a warm-pool API to preallocate worker slots and populate KV cache for selected model variants
Forecasting: a lightweight forecasting service that consumes 1-min and 5-min request traces and outputs a short-horizon demand curve per tenant/route
Policy Composer UI: console page to create policies binding tenant(s) -> {latency_budget_ms, cost_ceiling_per_min, fallback_model_priority, prewarm_thresholds}
Autoscaler integration: warm-pool controller should request prewarm actions and release actions via dedicated-scheduler APIs
Fallbacks: policy must support ordered fallbacks (same model lower-precision quant, lower-seq-length variant, different latency-optimized model) with automated routing
Observability: dashboards and alerts for warm-pool hit-rate, forecast accuracy, cost delta, and P99 latency by tenant
Billing: tag warm-pool compute and label it in usage reports separate from standard on-demand usage
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: Console policy can be created and applied to a test tenant; the warm-pool controller prewarms capacity when forecast exceeds threshold
Latency: For a controlled synthetic 10x burst, P99 first-token latency for the policy-bound tenant improves by at least 25% compared to baseline without warm pools
Cost: Warm-pool incremental cost for the test tenant remains <10% of the monthly cost baseline for the tenant during the validation window
Fallback correctness: When capacity intentionally limited, traffic is routed to fallback model variants in policy order and responses are served within declared latency budgets
Metrics: Forecast service provides confidence score; forecast accuracy (MAPE) for 0-15 minute horizon is <= 40% in the validation dataset
Observability: New dashboards surface warm-pool utilization, forecast delta, and cost tags; alerts fire when warm-pool hit-rate < 70% during expected burst windows
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood (alpha) — enable on staging tenants, validate forecast model and warm-pool APIs (4 weeks). Phase 2: Invite-only beta — 3 customers in staging and 2 in production with monitoring and billing tags (6 weeks). Phase 3: General availability — console UX polish, docs, pricing notes, and 24/7 oncall runbook (6 weeks). Each phase includes a canary rollback plan and a safety throttle: warm-pool controller capped at 10% of cluster spare capacity during beta.
success_metrics: % reduction in P99 first-token latency for bound tenants
Warm-pool cost as % of tenant spend
Number of incidents attributable to late prewarm actions, target = 0 in GA
risks: Forecast inaccuracy could cause wasted warm capacity or missed bursts
Billing attribution complexity may confuse customers and sales
Interaction with existing autoscale heuristics could cause thrashing if release thresholds misconfigured
Fallback routing to lower-quality variants could surface regressions for customers if not tested
open_questions: What default forecast model and retraining cadence is acceptable for alpha?
How should warm-pool costs be invoiced (line item vs amortized) to minimize customer surprise?
What safety caps should be enforced per-tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor prewarm abuse?
Should policies support schedule-based overrides (business hours) versus pure forecast-driven triggers?
